Published online:
    August 31, 2026

Geographic focus:
    United States (with geopolitical reference to Iran/Strait of Hormuz)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    Gold slid ~0.4% on Aug 31 to ~$4,433/oz, near a two-week low, pressured by hawkish Fed rhetoric from Chair Kevin Warsh at Jackson Hole, rising US yields, a stronger dollar, and surging oil prices amplifying inflation fears. Warsh signaled further rate hikes may be necessary if inflation doesn't return to the 2% target, triggering a 3%+ gold sell-off on Friday. September rate hike odds jumped to 64% from 36%. Markets now look to ADP and NFP data for direction. Silver, platinum, and palladium also declined on the day but remain strongly positive for the month.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?
Relevance: YES (US yields strengthening, dollar strengthening, Fed rate hike expectations, CME FedWatch pricing, NFP/ADP data all explicitly featured)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 90 (strongly centered on hawkish Fed pivot and rate hike expectations)
Probability of increase: 64% (directly cited from CME FedWatch Tool)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 10 (no meaningful discussion of a hold scenario; prior 36% pre-Warsh odds now largely displaced)
Probability of holding: 36%

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (rate cuts are not discussed or implied in any part of the article)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 80 (decidedly hawkish — Warsh's Jackson Hole signal, the jump in hike odds to 64%, stronger yields and dollar, and oil-driven inflation concerns all reinforce a more aggressive tightening bias with no dovish offsets present)
